correction: I asserted throughout the session that six positive labels were the binding constraint and that block was unmeasurable. Both were wrong: evals/golden/golden_events.jsonl holds 462 source-annotated events covering both games end to end, including 5 BLK.
why_bypassed: expected_moment_type is populated for only 100/462 rows because the golden set was built for highlight SELECTION, where misses/turnovers/rebounds are explicit negatives. For all-event DETECTION the signal is in source_event_type + source_outcome, which map onto the 14-label taxonomy exactly. The wrong field was being read.
conclusions_overturned: W2 turnover was never a false positive - it is a genuine golden TOV event
W2 assist is a real golden event, so the 051 anchoring bug cost a true positive
W6, excluded everywhere as qualitative, holds 5 golden events and the model recovers 2
block has 5 references, not 1, and is measurable

headline.interpretation: Every number reported before this was measured on seven windows selected because they contained human-reviewed events - a curated favourable sample that flattered the system by roughly 0.45 F1.

root_cause.finding: the model under-proposes: 9 predictions for 22 events across the new windows
root_cause.implication: The recall ceiling is at DISCOVERY, not classification. The verifier fix (044), rules gate (050), anchoring fix (051) and routing analysis (052) all operate downstream of a stage that is not proposing most of what happens.

still_standing: 044 verifier fix and 051 anchoring bug - both diagnosed from mechanism, not from the curated metric

next_action.step: fix proposer recall, then re-baseline every comparison on uncurated windows
next_action.cost_note: full game-1 video is local; discovery-only is ~$0.018/window, so ~$2 covers ~100 windows and several hundred references

limitations: the four new windows are game 1 only and deliberately the densest available, so 0.258 is a hard-case estimate; a random sample would likely fall between 0.258 and 0.706
